signal.summary: UberBond main now binds all 890 founder moonshots to a governed energy-compute-model-reality substrate mesh, activates a live GENESIS nursery, and routes new candidates through their moonshot ancestors.

candidates.title: Option-Constraint Eraser
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can identify constraints that reduce future options and distinguish removable friction from genuinely necessary boundaries.
candidates.mechanism: A constraint graph labels each limit by evidence, reversibility, external authority and downstream option loss, then proposes only internal or reversible removals.
candidates.falsifier: Proposed removals fail to expand measured option value or increase hidden risk/irreversibility.
candidates.nextProbe: Replay ten historical bottlenecks and compare proposed removals with actual later outcomes.

candidates.title: Laboratory Without Lab
candidates.hypothesis: A meaningful fraction of early scientific work can be moved into reproducible dry-lab simulation before scarce physical experiments are needed.
candidates.mechanism: The discovery grid compiles hypotheses into literature checks, formal models, simulations and computational falsifiers, escalating to wet-lab work only when uncertainty remains material.
candidates.falsifier: Dry-lab screening fails to eliminate low-value hypotheses better than a simple literature-only baseline.
candidates.nextProbe: Take five computationally tractable hypotheses and compare simulation-first versus literature-only filtering.

candidates.title: Compute Option Reservoir
candidates.hypothesis: Verified saved or shifted household energy can be treated as an option reserve that can be spent later on whichever local workload has the highest measured marginal value.
candidates.mechanism: UberWatt keeps energy as an unspent ledger asset until model/task benchmarks reveal the best verified progress per kWh.
candidates.falsifier: Immediate always-on compute produces equal or better long-run accepted progress than holding energy for higher-value jobs.
candidates.nextProbe: Compare a simulated reserve policy against always-run scheduling using measured task values and energy traces.

candidates.title: Experiment Market
candidates.hypothesis: Competing experiments can bid for scarce compute and review budget using expected information gain rather than queue order.
candidates.mechanism: Each experiment exposes falsifier, cost, expected uncertainty reduction and descendant unlocks; an internal market allocates a bounded research budget.
candidates.falsifier: Market-selected experiments reduce uncertainty no faster than FIFO or simple heuristic selection.
candidates.nextProbe: Backtest on a synthetic hypothesis graph with known answers, then shadow-run on internal research tasks.

candidates.title: Future Portfolio Treasury
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can preserve a diversified portfolio of possible futures instead of overcommitting compute, money or attention to one path.
candidates.mechanism: A portfolio layer tracks dependency concentration, reversibility and future-option coverage across active programs.
candidates.falsifier: Portfolio diversification lowers realized capability growth without meaningfully improving reversibility or option preservation.
candidates.nextProbe: Backtest on historical project branches and simulate concentration limits against realized downstream reuse.

candidates.title: Dusty Silicon Federation
candidates.hypothesis: Heterogeneous old laptops can contribute useful work by being treated as specialized cells rather than forced into one uniform cluster.
candidates.mechanism: A capability-aware scheduler benchmarks each node and assigns task classes where its marginal throughput per watt and reliability are competitive.
candidates.falsifier: The three-node federation yields no accepted-work throughput gain over using only the strongest HP after accounting for coordination cost.
candidates.nextProbe: Inventory both Lenovos, then benchmark three independent-worker modes against HP-only on identical bounded workloads.

candidates.title: Autonomous Failure-to-Patch Reflex
candidates.hypothesis: Repeated internal failures can be converted into bounded self-repair proposals before requiring a frontier model every time.
candidates.mechanism: Failure signatures map to known repair patterns, sandbox patches and regression tests; unknown patterns escalate instead of improvising.
candidates.falsifier: Automatic proposals create more regressions or frontier escalations than the existing manual repair path.
candidates.nextProbe: Replay a corpus of known repository failures with held-out variants and compare repair acceptance and regression rates.

candidates.title: Invisible Compute Fabric
candidates.hypothesis: Local compute can behave as a background utility without requiring the founder to manually select devices, models or queues.
candidates.mechanism: A zero-interface scheduler observes admitted node capabilities, task requirements and budgets, then routes only bounded internal jobs automatically.
candidates.falsifier: Automatic routing requires frequent manual correction or causes lower accepted throughput than explicit selection.
candidates.nextProbe: Run a week-equivalent replay from historical internal jobs and count manual intervention equivalents.

candidates.title: Blackout-First Compute Planner
candidates.hypothesis: The home compute mesh can be designed from failure states first so loss of power, network or a node never corrupts canonical work.
candidates.mechanism: Jobs are idempotent, checkpointed and independently receipted; graceful degradation preserves state and requeues unfinished work.
candidates.falsifier: Forced interruption causes duplicate effects, lost accepted work or unrecoverable state.
candidates.nextProbe: Fault-inject simulated power/network/node loss into a zero-effect job queue and verify exact replay behavior.

candidates.title: Home Compute Digital Twin
candidates.hypothesis: A digital twin of each laptop and the household compute envelope can forecast task runtime, heat, energy and reliability before scheduling.
candidates.mechanism: Measured node profiles feed a predictive model updated from benchmark receipts and external energy readings.
candidates.falsifier: Predictions remain too inaccurate to improve routing decisions compared with static benchmarks.
candidates.nextProbe: Collect repeated benchmark receipts and compare forecast error against simple rolling averages.

candidates.title: Founder-Choice Amplifier
candidates.hypothesis: Automation should increase the number and quality of meaningful choices surfaced to the founder while decreasing tactical burden.
candidates.mechanism: UberBond handles bounded execution and presents only consequential forks, uncertainty and reversible options at decision points.
candidates.falsifier: Automation reduces tactical work but also hides meaningful alternatives or increases irreversible commitments.
candidates.nextProbe: Replay major past decisions and compare information preserved by current versus choice-amplifying handoffs.

candidates.title: Thermodynamic Compute Scheduler
candidates.hypothesis: Compute scheduling can use measured energy and heat as first-class resource constraints rather than treating hardware throughput as the only objective.
candidates.mechanism: Jobs are routed using measured joules per accepted output, thermal headroom and latency, while safety ceilings remain externally sourced and fail closed.
candidates.falsifier: Energy-aware scheduling does not improve accepted progress per kWh or causes more throttling and instability.
candidates.nextProbe: Benchmark multiple bounded workloads with external energy measurement and compare throughput-only versus energy-aware schedules.
